text:
alex: FYI I'm seeing a spike of failing CI jobs after Dependabot pulled tokenizers 0.13.3 -> 0.14.0 and a new manylinux wheel rolled out. Failing on macOS runners and some linux images. stacktrace attached in logs below.

maria: Ugh. Any CVE or is this a build/regression from wheel ABI change?

alex: Not a reported CVE yet. Errors look like ``undefined symbol: _PyGen_Send`` from a compiled extension when importing tokenizers. Happens during pip install --no-binary :all: and when using the wheel.

sam: That symbol usually points at CPython ABI mismatch. Are builds targeting manylinux2014 vs manylinux2010? Which Python minor versions are failing?

alex: Fails on 3.9 and 3.10 in our runners. 3.11 on hosted mac is fine. CI logs: ```ERROR: tokenizers/_tokenizers.cpython-39-x86_64-linux-gnu.so: undefined symbol: _PyGen_Send```

jen: Could be tokenizers compiled against a newer CPython dev ABI. Did upstream change extension build flags? Any official release notes?

alex: changelog mentions wheel rebuilds for musl/manylinux variants. Not much detail. Dependabot PR shows bump from 0.13.3 to 0.14.0 and new binary wheels for linux.

maria: Short term mitigation: pin tokenizers to 0.13.3 in our constraints file so CI green while we triage. Longer term we need a policy for verifying wheels on our runners.

sam: +1 for constraints pin. For poetry projects we can add a constraints-style [tool.poetry.dependencies] override or vendor a lockfile patch. Which repos are failing? list?

alex: repo list: infra/llm-serving, api/python-client, examples/chatbot. I can open PRs to pin in pyproject.toml or add a constraints.txt for pip-based installs.

jen: Also add a test matrix job that installs with ``pip download tokenizers==0.14.0 --only-binary :all:`` on our runners to replicate. Might help us confirm wheel ABI mismatch.

ci-bot: deploy check-in: infra/llm-serving CI rerun started by alex at 2035001300.

dependabot-bot: Dependabot opened PR #812 bump tokenizers 0.13.3 -> 0.14.0 in api/python-client.

sam: For the poetry flow the minimal change is to regenerate the poetry.lock with current env (py3.9) and commit, but that could hide problem for customers on different platforms. I prefer constraints file in CI controlling manylinux tags.

maria: Security question: if we pin to older tokenizers, do we risk missing a real CVE fix? We need a check that the new version doesn't include security fixes we need.

alex: I scanned upstream release notes for 0.14.0 — no CVE/SECURITY mention. Looks like performance and wheel distribution changes. We'll still run a vuln scan of both versions.

jen: Triage plan proposal: 1) Hotfix: Add constraints pin to CI (tokenizers==0.13.3) and revert Dependabot where present. 2) Reproduce wheel import issue with ``pip download`` and a small repro docker image for manylinux2014 + python3.9. 3) Contact tokenizers maintainers + open issue with logs. 4) After maintainers respond, test their patched wheel. 5) If they don't respond in 72h escalate to internal patch (build from source in our pipeline).

sam: Agreed. Also update our security runbook: add a step to verify binary extensions across platforms when a new wheel lands. And we should add an audit log entry documenting the pin and the triage decisions (for later compliance review).

alex: I'll open the hotfix PR to add constraints.txt to CI and pin in pyproject where dependabot PRs exist. I'll include the repro commands: ``docker run --rm quay.io/pypa/manylinux2014_x86_64 bash -lc "python3.9 -m pip install tokenizers==0.14.0"``

maria: If we end up building from source in CI, we need to ensure our build uses the same compiler flags as upstream so ABI matches. Note for Private deployments we must validate the wheel before releasing to customer clusters — maybe a KMS/audit gating check?

jen: KMS mention: unrelated but if we rotate deployment keys for private clusters while rolling this fix, add a note to the incident ticket. Audit logs should capture who applied the pin and when.

alex: PRs up: infra/llm-serving #2203 (constraints.txt added), api/python-client #811 (revert dep bump + pin), examples/chatbot #412 (pin). CI green on linux after pin.

sam: Nice. Next: add a CI job that runs ``pip wheel tokenizers==0.14.0`` and then runs a small import test in a container to catch this earlier. Put that under eng-sre/regression matrix.
